texts.preamble: Smt.Kalpana vs Shri Nanjundaswamy on 3 September, 2019 In The Court Of Iii Addl.Judge And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Court Of Small Causes Bengaluru (Scch-18) Dated: This the 3rd day of September 2019 Present: Sri.Mahantesh S.Dargad B.Sc., LL.B.,(Spl) Iii Addl. Judge & Member, Mact Court Of Small Causes, Bengaluru. M.V.C.No.2398/2018 Petitioner Smt.Kalpana, Wife of Bore Gowda, Aged about 43 years, Resident of Allenhalli, Gubbi Taluk, Kadaba, Tumkur District. (By Pleader Shri M.Manjunath) V/s. Respondents 1.Shri Nanjundaswamy, C/o Allen Paul, No.33, Blessed Cottage, Vsr Layout, Kadugudi, Bengaluru-560 067. (R.C.Owner of the car bearing No.KA-53- Me-5829) (By Pleader Shri A.T.Nagendra) 2 Scch-18 Mvc 2398/2018 2.The Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co.Ltd., No.25/1, 2nd floor, Building No.2, Shankara Narayana building, M.G. road, Bengaluru-560 001. Represented by its Manager (Policy No.2311201940787600000 valid from 11.10.2017 to 10.10.2018) (By Pleader Shri Madhukiran) Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95839367/ 1 J U D G M E N T
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.30,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the petition are as under: On 7.4.2018 at about 3.30 p.m. the petitioner was traveling along with her family members from Hassan towards Tumkur in a car bearing No.KA-53-ME-5829, which was driven by one Nanjundaswamy with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human lie and safety of others, when he reached near Joddagatte Rajesh Dhaba, Bidar to Srirangapatna road, Turuvekere in order to avoid oncoming lorry he suddenly took the left and dashed against the road side tree. Due to the said impact, the car was severely damaged and the petitioner and her family members sustained grievous injuries. Immediately she was shifted to Adichunchanagiri hospital, further she was shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was treated as inpatient. 3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 43 years, doing agriculture and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month. The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-53-ME-5829. Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation. Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost. 4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared through their counsel, but inspite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement , so, the written statement of the respondent No.1 is taken as not filed. The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement. 5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under: The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts. Further admitted about the issuance of the policy and its validity from 11.10.2017 to 10.10.2018 and the policy is having coverage only for limited liability. 7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner herself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P15 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P16 & Ex.P17. 8. To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 has not examined any witness on their behalf.
texts.arguments: Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars. Further contended that driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident. Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition. Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost. Further he argued that, to prove the disablement, the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW2, who has assessed the disability of 89% of left lower limb and 29% of whole body. Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence. Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition. 12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has denied the accident in toto, hence, prays to dismiss the petition. 16. The counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that the alleged vehicle was not involved in the accident. On the other hand, the petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence. 17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others). 24. The contention of the petitioner is that, she has spent huge amount of Rs.15,00,000/- towards medical expenses. 25. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, aged about 43 years, doing agriculture and earning Rs.20,000/- per month. 29. Further contention of the petitioner is that she has sustained grievous injuries.
